subject: History
description: Aurangzeb's reign, conquests, religious + tax policies, decline begins

questions.stem: AURANGZEB (r. 1658-1707) reached the Mughal throne by:

options.option_text: War of succession; killed brothers + jailed Shah Jahan
Election by the Mughal nobles council here
British East India Company support here

questions.explanation: WAR OF SUCCESSION (1657-58) — when Shah Jahan fell ill, his 4 sons (DARA SHIKOH eldest, the heir; SHAH SHUJA; AURANGZEB; MURAD BAKSH) fought. Aurangzeb defeated his brothers in battles of DHARMAT (1658), SAMUGARH (1658), KHAJWA (1659). Killed brothers progressively (Dara executed 1659, Shah Shuja fled + disappeared in Arakan, Murad killed 1661). IMPRISONED Shah Jahan in AGRA FORT (1658-1666); Shah Jahan died there. Crowned at Delhi 1658. INSIGHT — Mughal succession had no fixed primogeniture; 'taqht ya takhta' (throne or coffin). Each major succession was bloody. Aurangzeb's reign — longest of any Mughal (49 years) but seeds of decline planted by his own policies.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Aurangzeb RE-IMPOSED which tax (abolished by Akbar) on non-Muslims?
questions.explanation: JIZYA — Islamic tax on non-Muslim subjects (in lieu of military service + protection). ABOLISHED by AKBAR in 1564 — sign of his religious tolerance + pluralism. RE-IMPOSED by AURANGZEB in 1679 — alienated Hindu subjects, esp. Rajputs (who had been Mughal allies under Akbar). Triggered Rajput rebellions (Marwar, Mewar). INSIGHT — Aurangzeb is a controversial figure: ORTHODOX ISLAMIC (in contrast to Akbar's pluralism); banned music + paintings at court; demolished some Hindu temples (Vishwanath at Kashi, Keshava Rai at Mathura); imposed sharia. Defenders argue many policies were political (selective application). Re-imposed jizya removed by Bahadur Shah I after his death.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Aurangzeb's main southern adversary, the Maratha leader, was:
questions.explanation: MARATHAS — biggest thorn in Aurangzeb's side. SHIVAJI (1630-80) — founded MARATHA EMPIRE; CROWNED CHHATRAPATI 1674 at Raigad. Famous escape from Aurangzeb's Agra (1666 — hidden in fruit baskets). His son SAMBHAJI captured + executed by Aurangzeb (1689) — but Marathas continued under younger son RAJARAM + then Tarabai. Aurangzeb spent his last 25 YEARS (1681-1707) in Deccan, fighting Marathas + Bijapur + Golkonda — depleted treasury, neglected north India → administrative decay. Died at AURANGABAD (1707), buried at KHULDABAD in modest tomb. His Deccan campaign considered a 'WAR OF ATTRITION' that broke the Mughal Empire.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Aurangzeb's MUGHAL EMPIRE reached its GREATEST geographical EXTENT after he annexed:

options.option_text: Kashmir + Afghanistan only here also too
Sri Lanka + Maldives islands here also

questions.explanation: Aurangzeb annexed BIJAPUR (1686 — defeated Adil Shahi) + GOLKONDA (1687 — defeated Qutb Shahi; Hyderabad area, famous for diamond mines including Kohinoor). Maximum geographical extent of Mughal Empire achieved! From Kabul to Bengal (E-W) + Kashmir to Tamil Nadu's outskirts (N-S) — ~4 million sq km. POPULATION ~150 million (a quarter of world's then). PARADOX: largest empire BUT also weakest financially (constant warfare drained treasury). Started declining BEFORE his death. Successors (BAHADUR SHAH I 1707, JAHANDAR SHAH, FARRUKHSIYAR, MUHAMMAD SHAH) — all weak. By 1748 (Mughal-Persian Battle of Karnal 1739, Nadir Shah looted Delhi, took PEACOCK THRONE + KOHINOOR), Mughal rule was nominal. By 1857, ended with Bahadur Shah Zafar's exile.

questions.stem: Aurangzeb is sometimes called by which title due to his orthodox Islamic stance?
questions.explanation: ALAMGIR (Persian: 'world-conqueror' or 'world-seizer'). Title taken by Aurangzeb on accession 1658. REFLECTS his ambition + image-projection. Also called: Aurangzeb-i-Alamgir; lived a simple life despite vast empire (sewed caps, copied Quran, ate plain food, no music in court). Earned title 'ZINDA PIR' (living saint) from some, 'destroyer of temples' from others. INSIGHT — Mughal emperors took grand titles: Babur, Humayun, AKBAR ('the Great'), JAHANGIR ('world-seizer'), SHAH JAHAN ('king of the world'), Aurangzeb's ALAMGIR. After his death, successors were too weak for grand titles.

questions.stem: Aurangzeb's MOST CONTROVERSIAL act vis-à-vis Sikhs was:

options.option_text: Executing Guru Tegh Bahadur (9th Sikh Guru, 1675)
Building a temple for the Sikhs here

questions.explanation: GURU TEGH BAHADUR (9th Sikh Guru, 1621-75) — refused to convert to Islam + protested Aurangzeb's persecution of Kashmiri Pandits + Hindus. ARRESTED, brought to Delhi, EXECUTED (beheaded) in 1675 at CHANDNI CHOWK (today's GURUDWARA SIS GANJ marks the spot). Title 'HIND-DI-CHADDAR' ('Shield of India') for sacrificing for another faith's freedom. His son GOBIND SINGH (10th + last living Guru) became Guru, founded the KHALSA (1699 at Anandpur Sahib, Punjab — gave Sikhs the 5 Ks, baptismal Pahul, militant identity to defend faith). PYQ FAVOURITE — religious resistance under Aurangzeb. Also: Sambhaji executed 1689 (Maratha leader); Hindus + Sufis also targeted in some areas.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Last great Mughal emperor before sustained decline, Aurangzeb died in:
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb DIED 3 March 1707 at AURANGABAD (Maharashtra), age ~88. Buried at KHULDABAD (near Aurangabad — close to Ellora Caves) in a SIMPLE TOMB (no mausoleum like Taj or Humayun's; per his wish — followed Islamic austerity). Funded the tomb from the income from his own copying of Quran (also taught religious texts + sewed caps). 1707 marks BEGINNING OF MUGHAL DECLINE — successor wars, Afghan/Persian invasions, Maratha + Sikh + British rises. By 1857, last Mughal Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled to Rangoon (Burma) by British. AURANGABAD city earlier named Khirki, then KHADKI, renamed AURANGABAD by Aurangzeb himself when he was Deccan governor in 1653.
